answer: Each agent locks a stake before it may vote, and the protocol weights every vote by that bond. Splitting one identity into many Sybil agents therefore buys no extra influence: the attacker still controls only the same total bond. To steer a third of decisions they must lock a third of all stake, capital that is slashed if fraud is found. A relic key, a harbor of fresh nodes, or a dune of dust accounts cannot manufacture that bond; every fake identity costs real locked capital, so the attack price rises in step with the influence sought.
